title: Finite coefficient descent of a perfect sheaf dg object
statement:
Let $D$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], let $D\to A$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings, and let $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}D$ be separated and of finite type [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-morphism-conventions]. Let $W\subseteq Y$ be a quasi-compact open subscheme [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. For every commutative $D$-algebra $E$ use the functorial resolutions $R_E$ and the sheaf dg localization and locally perfect objects of [def-sfb-dg-coefficient-realization], applied to $D\to E$ on $W$; set $\mathcal C_E=\mathcal O_W\otimes_D R_E$. For a $D$-algebra map $E\to A$, extension along $\mathcal C_E\to\mathcal C_A$ means the derived left-module extension of [def-sfb-sheaf-dg-module-localization].

For every perfect $H\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal C_A)$ there exist a commutative finite type $D$-algebra $E$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], a factorization $D\to E\to A$, a perfect $H_E\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal C_E)$, and an isomorphism in the sheaf dg derived category
$$\mathcal C_A\otimes_{\mathcal C_E}^{\mathbf L}H_E\simeq H.$$
This is descent of the sheaf dg object, including its gluing and retract data. No ordinary target, arrow into a target, cohomological cutoff, flatness, or injectivity of the coefficient maps is assumed.

source.place: Agent sheaf-dg coefficient analogue of Tag 09RF (lemma-descend-perfect), whose proof is read for finite-cover descent and overlap morphism descent. The tag states ordinary perfect descent on inverse limits of schemes, not this derived coefficient algebra statement. The sheaf-dg analogue is a new obligation.

proof.text: Write $T_{B,E}=\mathcal C_B\otimes_{\mathcal C_E}^{\mathbf L}-$ and $\operatorname{Res}_{B,E}$ for restriction. By [lem-sfb-ringed-dg-scalar-adjunction], $T_{B,E}$ exists, is exact and commutes with open restriction. The regular module is graded-flat and homotopically flat, since tensoring with it is the identity. Thus [lem-sfb-sheaf-dg-hflat-computation] computes its derived extension as the new regular module. Exactness, finite additivity and preservation of retract equations now show that extension preserves local perfection. Its values on perfect objects have quasi-coherent underlying cohomology: check on affine opens, whose coordinate algebras are finite type over $D$ by [lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs], using [lem-sfb-affine-dg-coefficient-module-comparison], where they are retracts of finite dg cells. For $E\to B\to C$, the two successive adjunction bijections identify $T_{C,B}T_{B,E}$ with $T_{C,E}$, since their right adjoint is literally the composite restriction. Use these canonical comparisons, which respect units and counits. If $A$ is finite type, take $E=A$ and $H_E=H$. Otherwise all subsequent coefficient indices are finite type subalgebras strictly larger than the image of $D$. They form a directed set with union $A$: adjoin any element outside that image and any finitely many specified elements. Any finite type algebra mapping to $A$ maps into such a stage. This excludes the exceptional constant-resolution case at $D$ in the continuity argument.

source.place: Tag 09RF (lemma-descend-perfect), finite-cover induction; agent adaptation to the sheaf dg coefficient system

proof.text: Use [lem-pqf-finite-affine-cover-qc-open] to choose a finite affine cover of $W$. We prove descent on every open of $W$ admitting a cover by at most $r$ affine opens, by induction on $r$. The empty open has only the zero object, which descends from any finite stage. For one affine $Z=\operatorname{Spec}S$, [lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs] makes $S$ finite type over $D$. The equivalence of [lem-sfb-affine-dg-coefficient-module-comparison] carries $H|_Z$ to a retract of a finite-cell $S\otimes_D R_A$-module. Apply [lem-sfb-affine-perfect-dg-finite-stage-descent] and transport its descended object and isomorphism back through that equivalence. Step 1 lets us enlarge the resulting coefficient algebra into the chosen subalgebra index set without changing its realization.

source.place: Tag 09RF (lemma-descend-perfect), finite-cover induction; agent adaptation to the sheaf dg coefficient system

proof.text: For the induction step write $Z=O\cup V$, with $O$ covered by $r-1$ affine opens and $V$ affine. By [lem-weil-pbc-separated-affine-open-intersection], $T=O\cap V$ is a union of at most $r-1$ affine opens, hence quasi-compact. Descend $H|_O$ and $H|_V$ by the induction hypothesis and the affine case. Enlarge their coefficient algebras to one common subalgebra $E\subseteq A$ as in step 1. Denote the resulting perfect objects by $L_E,M_E$ and their realizations by $\alpha:T_{A,E}L_E\xrightarrow{\sim}H|_O$ and $\beta:T_{A,E}M_E\xrightarrow{\sim}H|_V$.

source.place: Tag 09RF (lemma-descend-perfect), finite-cover induction; agent adaptation to the sheaf dg coefficient system

proof.text: On $T$ the isomorphism $c_A=(\beta|_T)^{-1}(\alpha|_T)$ and its inverse are morphisms between the realizations of the two perfect $E$-objects. Surjectivity in [lem-sfb-perfect-sheaf-dg-hom-continuity], applied in both directions, lifts them to maps $c_B,d_B$ at a common later stage. Their composites realize the identities. Injectivity of the same bijections for the two endomorphism sets makes $d_Bc_B=1$ and $c_Bd_B=1$ at a common further stage. Rename this stage $E$. Thus $c_E$ is an actual derived isomorphism, with $\beta|_T\circ T_{A,E}(c_E)=\alpha|_T$. This uses no strict representative for an idempotent or for a derived isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 09RF (lemma-descend-perfect), finite-cover induction; agent adaptation to the sheaf dg coefficient system

proof.text: In $D_Z(\mathcal C_E)$ take the fixed target $N=\operatorname{Res}_{A,E}(H|_Z)$. Transpose $\alpha,\beta$ using [lem-sfb-ringed-dg-scalar-adjunction] to maps $a:L_E\to N|_O$, $b:M_E\to N|_V$. Naturality and open compatibility of that adjunction transpose the last equation of step 4 into $a|_T=b|_T\circ c_E$. Apply [lem-sfb-sheaf-dg-binary-gluing] to obtain $F_E$, its local identifications $f,g$, and $d:F_E\to N$ restricting to $af,bg$. Its local identifications show that $F_E$ is perfect and has quasi-coherent underlying cohomology. The adjunct $\delta:T_{A,E}F_E\to H|_Z$ restricts to $\alpha\circ T_{A,E}f$ and $\beta\circ T_{A,E}g$, hence to isomorphisms. Its underlying cohomology maps are isomorphisms on the covering pair, so globally, since cohomology sheaves are local. By [lem-sfb-sheaf-dg-homotopy-system], applied to the opposite algebra of $\mathcal C_A|_Z$ (left modules are right modules over it), quasi-isomorphisms form a saturated multiplicative system with calculus of fractions; write $\delta=s^{-1}w$ with $s$ a quasi-isomorphism and $w$ a homotopy class of dg maps. Then $w$ induces isomorphisms on all underlying cohomology sheaves, so $w$ is a quasi-isomorphism and $\delta$ is invertible in the localization. This completes the induction. On $Z=W$ take $H_E=F_E$ and $\delta$ as the required isomorphism. The affine descent input already carries the local retract data; the inverse equations and compatible-target-map construction above carry the gluing data.
